record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Let S4u be the topological modal logic S4 with a universal modality, interpreted over topological spaces. What is the logical behavior of the extension of S4u by the metric distance operators exists<=a and exists>a?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the modal logic S4u, defined as the propositional modal logic S4 (with modal operators □ and ◇) augmented with a universal modality ∀ (and its dual ∃), interpreted on topological spaces in the standard topological semantics: □ is interpreted as the topological interior operator, and ∀φ holds at a point of a space X iff φ holds at every point of X.

Now extend the language of S4u by adding, for each positive rational number a, two binary "metric distance" operators:
- ∃^{≤a}: for a formula φ, the formula ∃^{≤a}φ holds at a point x of a metric space (X,d) iff there exists y ∈ X with d(x,y) ≤ a such that φ holds at y;
- ∃^{>a}: similarly, ∃^{>a}φ holds at x iff there exists y ∈ X with d(x,y) > a such that φ holds at y.

Models are metric spaces (X,d) with a valuation of propositional variables, and the topological connectives of S4u are interpreted via the metric topology induced by d.

Determine the logical behaviour of this extension of S4u by the operators ∃^{≤a} and ∃^{>a}: in particular, provide a complete and sound axiomatization of the set of formulas valid in all metric spaces, and determine the decidability and computational complexity of its satisfiability/validity problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work by Kutz, Wolter, Sturm, Zakharyaschev and others studies modal "distance logics" with operators of the form ∃^{≤a} and ∃^{>a} over distance spaces, and several axiomatization and decidability results exist for fragments. However, no source clearly settles the specific question of axiomatizing and determining the decidability/complexity of S4u extended by these metric operators interpreted on metric spaces; the problem appears to remain open in the published literature.

status_evidence.title: A modal logic framework for reasoning about comparative distances and topology
status_evidence.snippet: Modal languages for talking about distances interpreted in distance spaces, with results on decidability and axiomatization of certain combined topology+distance logics.
status_evidence.claim: Distance operators ∃^{≤a}, ∃^{>a} have been studied with topological modalities, but the combination with S4u remains a nontrivial open direction.

status_evidence.title: Axiomatizing Distance Logics
status_evidence.snippet: Axiomatizations for several modal logics of distance with operators of the form ∃^{≤a} and ∃^{>a}.
status_evidence.claim: Partial axiomatization results exist for distance operators alone, but extensions to S4u with topological interior have not been fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Logics of Metric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/notes on modal logics for metric spaces, listing open problems concerning interactions of topological and metric modalities.
status_evidence.claim: The combination of S4u with metric distance operators is identified as an open problem.
